design.question: Among US counties declared in the same FEMA major disaster (severe storm, flood or tornado), how does county employment as first published change over the following 3, 6, 12 and 24 months in counties in the top decile of recorded damage per resident relative to declared counties where almost no damage was recorded, comparing counties that were on similar employment paths beforehand?

treatment.absorbing: a stack's treated county stays treated; later disasters are part of its post-period path
treatment.design_stage_counts: 9,336 (disaster, county) pairs of the four types with an incident beginning 2009-05..2024-07; 5,955 dropped for another qualifying DR in the previous 36 months; 19 without BEA population; 3,362 pairs remain across 451 disasters, of which 1,759 have a strictly positive recorded dose. At the pinned threshold: 176 treated, 1,903 control, 1,283 in the excluded middle. Dose percentiles over damaged pairs: p50 $13.91, p75 $65.85, p90 $302.79, p95 $935.18, p99 $4,155.97.
treatment.dose: sum of NOAA storm_damage_property + storm_damage_crops (nominal USD) over county-coded storm events in the declared county whose begin date falls in [incident_begin_date, incident_end_date], divided by the county's BEA population in calendar year (g // 12) - 1
treatment.dose_incident_types_reason: Unchanged from wave 2: NOAA records these hazards against counties, while hurricane, tropical-storm, winter and heat damage is recorded against NWS forecast zones and cannot be attributed to a county, so a 'zero-damage' control inside a hurricane declaration could in fact be heavily damaged.
treatment.dose_quantile_reason: The quantile is taken over damaged pairs, not over all declared pairs, so the threshold is a statement about damaged counties and does not move when a declaration happens to include many undamaged ones. Over all in-scope pairs the 90th percentile is $114.66, which is wave 2's $100 threshold by another name and not a larger contrast; over damaged pairs it is $302.79.
treatment.dose_rule: treated = dose at or above the 90th percentile of the dose distribution over in-scope (disaster, county) pairs with a strictly positive recorded dose; control = dose below $1 per resident; pairs between the two are excluded
treatment.dose_timing: Damage is estimated by NWS offices from the physical event within weeks: a property of the shock, measured after it, but not derived from any employment outcome. As in wave 2 this is a disclosed use of an ex-post intensity, and the assumption that damage is not predicted by the county's employment path is what the leads test.
treatment.estimated_cohort_months_reason: The monthly first-release panel has national coverage from reference month 2007-05 and runs to 2026-07. A cohort needs its matching window at g-24 and its longest horizon at g+24, so 2009-05 is the earliest datable cohort and 2024-07 the latest. Every horizon is estimated on this one cohort set, so the four horizons are comparable rather than four different samples.
treatment.quiet_period_rule: a (disaster, county) pair is dropped when the county has another qualifying DR whose incident begins in the 36 months before g; other disasters in the same month or later are part of the post-period path
treatment.source: event_library: library_type fema_major_disaster_declaration (county rows, 50 states + DC); dose from noaa_storm_events county-coded damage; population from bea_national_regional CAINC1
treatment.timing: g = the calendar month of the disaster's incident_begin_date, indexed year * 12 + (month - 1)
treatment.treated_min_usd_per_capita_measured: Measured on treatment-side data only (FEMA declarations, NOAA county damage, BEA population) before any outcome was read. Pinned here as a number so that the design does not move if the sample does.

units.definition: (disaster, county) pairs: each disaster is a stack holding its treated and control counties; a county may appear in several stacks
units.notes: County definitional changes are not bridged. The two FRED aliases for Hancock County, KY are one county in the outcome panel, which keeps the earlier of the two releases for a month.
units.sample: units need the outcome in month g-24 and month g-13; others are dropped
units.strata: disaster x pre-growth half: comparisons are only within the same disaster and the same half of the outcome's growth from g-24 to g-13 (split at the median of the disaster's treated and control counties by (growth, id) rank)
units.strata_differs_from_wave_2: Wave 2 matched every outcome on employment growth. Here each outcome is matched on its own growth from g-24 to g-13, as units.strata says, so the secondary outcomes sit on partly different unit sets from the primary one and their samples are reported separately. This is the sample the power measurement was computed on, so it is kept rather than changed after the fact; the cost is that a secondary outcome is not a decomposition of the primary one.
units.unit_window: each unit's series is clipped to event months -24..+24 around its own stack's declaration month. Every unit belongs to exactly one declaration and every unit in a stack shares that declaration's month, so a month outside that window can enter no group-time cell this design estimates; the clip is exact, not an approximation.

windows.bounding_only_reason: Stated explicitly so no reader and no runner has to infer it from power.measured. It agrees with power.measured.verdict.can_only_bound_at, and the runner raises if the two ever disagree. Their minimum detectable effects clear 0.02, but the test rejects a true null 11.5% of the time at both, past the power registration's 10% limit, so no rejection at these horizons may be reported as an effect.
windows.e_min_reason: Leads e = -6..-2 are the gating pre-trend window, chosen on measured size before registration; see power.measured.diagnostics.why_the_lead_window_is_six_months. The matching window ends at g-13, so it still ends before every tested lead.
windows.horizons_note: All four horizons are estimated on the same cohort set and the same panel. The primary estimand is the mean ATT over event months 0..6: it is the longest horizon at which the design is both powered against the effect worth finding and correctly sized (measured minimum detectable effect 0.0116 against 0.02, rejection rate under a true null 9.0% against a 10% limit). The 3-month horizon is reported beside it. The 12- and 24-month horizons are registered as BOUNDING ONLY: their minimum detectable effects also clear 0.02, but the test rejects a true null 11.5% of the time at both, so no rejection at those horizons may be reported as an effect and their intervals must be read as wider than they print.

overall.definition: equal-weight mean of ATT(e) over the post event times listed

does_not_establish: Coverage before reference month 2007-05 is the Federal Reserve Eighth District, not the nation, which is why no cohort before 2009-05 is estimated: its matching window would fall in months when only seven states were in the archive.
A monthly outcome raises the number of periods, not the number of states. Inference is clustered on state, so the design's precision is bounded by roughly 50 clusters however many months it holds.

BOUNDING ONLY, never an effect, at these horizons: 12 months 11.5%, 24 months 11.5%. Those are the rates at which this design rejects a true null, measured before registration on synthetic panels with no effect in them, against a 10% limit. The intervals printed for those horizons are therefore narrower than their true coverage and must be read as wider than they print, and a rejection at them is not an effect and is not reported as one here. The registered primary estimand is the mean ATT over event months 0..6, the longest horizon at which this design is both powered against the effect worth finding and correctly sized.

assumptions: Parallel trends: absent treatment, the average outcome of treated units would have moved like that of the comparison units (not-yet-treated or never-treated, within stratum when stratified) from the base period on.
No anticipation beyond the registered anticipation window: outcomes before g - anticipation do not respond.
Absorbing treatment: the first qualifying event defines the cohort; later events are part of the post-period treatment path, so estimates are effects of entering treatment, not of one isolated event.
SUTVA / no interference: a unit's outcome does not depend on other units' treatment (spillovers to comparison units bias the estimate toward zero or away from it).
Treatment timing is recorded correctly by the source date the registration names.

Within a declaration and a pre-growth half, which counties NOAA records as heavily damaged is unrelated to their employment path: storm paths, not local economic conditions, decide where damage falls.
NOAA county-coded damage measures the physical damage with error unrelated to the employment path; unreported damage in 'control' counties biases the estimate toward zero.
Nominal damage thresholds are applied across 2009-2024 without deflation (prices rose about 45%), so the treated group in later years includes relatively smaller real damage.

LAUS county employment is partly modelled: BLS builds county estimates from a state model and disaggregates them, so a county-specific shock may be smoothed toward its state. This attenuates any real effect and is the main reason a monthly LAUS outcome may be less sensitive than its frequency suggests. The wave-1 cyclone exposure test named the same property as a reason its ranking may have failed.
First releases are noisier than later vintages: the outcome is what was known then, which is the point, and it is not the best estimate of what happened.

The outcome is not seasonally adjusted, so seasonality is absorbed by the stratum-by-month comparison rather than by the series; the design compares counties in the same declaration and therefore in the same calendar months.
Spillovers from heavily damaged to lightly damaged counties of the same disaster (commuting, reconstruction demand) are small; they would bias the estimate toward zero.
The estimand is the effect of top-decile relative to negligible damage given a declaration; it is not the effect of the declaration or of federal aid.
identification.estimand: ATT: equal-weight mean over event months 0..H of treated-count-weighted ATT(g, g+e), for top-decile-damage declared counties relative to negligible-damage counties of the same declaration. H = 6 is primary; H = 3 is reported beside it; H = 12 and H = 24 are reported as bounds only (see windows.horizons_note).
identification.label: did_failed_diagnostics
identification.meaning: A difference-in-differences estimate whose pre-registered diagnostics failed. It is reported for transparency and must not be read as an intervention response.

notes: The registration dates its cohort and calendar windows as YYYY-MM and states its primary estimand as a horizon in months. The runner resolves those mechanically - months to period indices year * 12 + (month - 1), and the primary horizon to the post window 0..primary_horizon_months - and derives nothing else: treatment.estimated_cohorts and windows.post in the recorded design are those two resolutions of the registration as written.

estimates.horizons holds every registered horizon on the same cohort set and the same panel. The row for the primary horizon is the primary estimate; rows the registration registered as bounds carry bounding_only, the size that made them bounds, and the sentence that says a rejection there is not an effect. The identification label and the verdict follow from the primary horizon alone.

estimates.robustness_roles says which robustness estimate can gate the identification label. An estimate gates only where an acceptance criterion reads a fact it produces; the criteria are the registration's own and the runner adds, removes and alters none. The pre-trend criterion is the joint Wald test over the gating lead window windows.e_min..-2; the longer lead window is estimated and reported as a non-gating variant, and no criterion can see it.
results.verdict: No causal claim. Pre-registered diagnostics failed (no_pre_trends), so the parallel-trends design is not credible here. The estimate for log LAUS county employment as first published: log(civilian labour force x (1 - unemployment rate / 100)), +0.0034 log points (95% CI -0.0018 to +0.0085), is reported only for transparency.

assumptions: Parallel trends: absent treatment, the average outcome of treated units would have moved like that of the comparison units (not-yet-treated or never-treated, within stratum when stratified) from the base period on.
No anticipation beyond the registered anticipation window: outcomes before g - anticipation do not respond.
Absorbing treatment: the first qualifying event defines the cohort; later events are part of the post-period treatment path, so estimates are effects of entering treatment, not of one isolated event.
SUTVA / no interference: a unit's outcome does not depend on other units' treatment (spillovers to comparison units bias the estimate toward zero or away from it).
Treatment timing is recorded correctly by the source date the registration names.

Within a declaration and a pre-growth half, which counties NOAA records as heavily damaged is unrelated to their employment path: storm paths, not local economic conditions, decide where damage falls.
NOAA county-coded damage measures the physical damage with error unrelated to the employment path; unreported damage in 'control' counties biases the estimate toward zero.
Nominal damage thresholds are applied across 2009-2024 without deflation (prices rose about 45%), so the treated group in later years includes relatively smaller real damage.

LAUS county employment is partly modelled: BLS builds county estimates from a state model and disaggregates them, so a county-specific shock may be smoothed toward its state. This attenuates any real effect and is the main reason a monthly LAUS outcome may be less sensitive than its frequency suggests. The wave-1 cyclone exposure test named the same property as a reason its ranking may have failed.
First releases are noisier than later vintages: the outcome is what was known then, which is the point, and it is not the best estimate of what happened.

The outcome is not seasonally adjusted, so seasonality is absorbed by the stratum-by-month comparison rather than by the series; the design compares counties in the same declaration and therefore in the same calendar months.
Spillovers from heavily damaged to lightly damaged counties of the same disaster (commuting, reconstruction demand) are small; they would bias the estimate toward zero.
The estimand is the effect of top-decile relative to negligible damage given a declaration; it is not the effect of the declaration or of federal aid.
identification.estimand: ATT: equal-weight mean over event months 0..H of treated-count-weighted ATT(g, g+e), for top-decile-damage declared counties relative to negligible-damage counties of the same declaration. H = 6 is primary; H = 3 is reported beside it; H = 12 and H = 24 are reported as bounds only (see windows.horizons_note).
identification.label: did_failed_diagnostics
identification.meaning: A difference-in-differences estimate whose pre-registered diagnostics failed. It is reported for transparency and must not be read as an intervention response.

notes: The registration dates its cohort and calendar windows as YYYY-MM and states its primary estimand as a horizon in months. The runner resolves those mechanically - months to period indices year * 12 + (month - 1), and the primary horizon to the post window 0..primary_horizon_months - and derives nothing else: treatment.estimated_cohorts and windows.post in the recorded design are those two resolutions of the registration as written.

estimates.horizons holds every registered horizon on the same cohort set and the same panel. The row for the primary horizon is the primary estimate; rows the registration registered as bounds carry bounding_only, the size that made them bounds, and the sentence that says a rejection there is not an effect. The identification label and the verdict follow from the primary horizon alone.

estimates.robustness_roles says which robustness estimate can gate the identification label. An estimate gates only where an acceptance criterion reads a fact it produces; the criteria are the registration's own and the runner adds, removes and alters none. The pre-trend criterion is the joint Wald test over the gating lead window windows.e_min..-2; the longer lead window is estimated and reported as a non-gating variant, and no criterion can see it.
results.verdict: No causal claim. Pre-registered diagnostics failed (no_pre_trends, placebo_unit_size), so the parallel-trends design is not credible here. The estimate for log LAUS civilian labour force as first published, +0.0018 log points (95% CI -0.0025 to +0.0060), is reported only for transparency.

primary.construction: LAUS publishes employment as an identity on these two series, and the monthly county employed series with a deep ALFRED archive does not exist (the structured LAUCN form opens only in 2019). A month enters only when the county has a first release of both features for it, and the month's availability is the later of the two vintages.
primary.label: log LAUS county employment as first published: log(civilian labour force x (1 - unemployment rate / 100))
primary.why_primary: It is the monthly analogue of wave 2's primary outcome, so the effect worth finding carries over to it unchanged.

secondary.label: log LAUS civilian labour force as first published
secondary.why: the same denominator without the rate, so a reader can see how much of the employment series is participation rather than unemployment

secondary.label: LAUS county unemployment rate as first published
secondary.why: not logged; the effect worth finding for employment does not apply to it and it is reported in its own units

outcomes.transform: natural log of positive values for the two log outcomes; the rate is used in levels; months without a first release of both features are absent, not zero

placebo_date.definition: treated units keep only months before g; placebo cohort g-6; placebo effect averaged over placebo event months 0..5, all of which precede the declaration

placebo_unit.definition: real treated units removed; control counties receive cohorts drawn from their stratum's real cohorts at the stratum's real treated share
placebo_unit.post_window: the primary post window, event months 0..6, so the placebo rejection rate is the size of the test that gates the primary estimand

design.question: Among US counties declared in the same FEMA major disaster (severe storm, flood or tornado), how does county employment as first published change over the following 3, 6, 12 and 24 months in counties in the top decile of recorded damage per resident relative to declared counties where almost no damage was recorded, comparing counties that were on similar employment paths beforehand?

treatment.absorbing: a stack's treated county stays treated; later disasters are part of its post-period path
treatment.design_stage_counts: 9,336 (disaster, county) pairs of the four types with an incident beginning 2009-05..2024-07; 5,955 dropped for another qualifying DR in the previous 36 months; 19 without BEA population; 3,362 pairs remain across 451 disasters, of which 1,759 have a strictly positive recorded dose. At the pinned threshold: 176 treated, 1,903 control, 1,283 in the excluded middle. Dose percentiles over damaged pairs: p50 $13.91, p75 $65.85, p90 $302.79, p95 $935.18, p99 $4,155.97.
treatment.dose: sum of NOAA storm_damage_property + storm_damage_crops (nominal USD) over county-coded storm events in the declared county whose begin date falls in [incident_begin_date, incident_end_date], divided by the county's BEA population in calendar year (g // 12) - 1
treatment.dose_incident_types_reason: Unchanged from wave 2: NOAA records these hazards against counties, while hurricane, tropical-storm, winter and heat damage is recorded against NWS forecast zones and cannot be attributed to a county, so a 'zero-damage' control inside a hurricane declaration could in fact be heavily damaged.
treatment.dose_quantile_reason: The quantile is taken over damaged pairs, not over all declared pairs, so the threshold is a statement about damaged counties and does not move when a declaration happens to include many undamaged ones. Over all in-scope pairs the 90th percentile is $114.66, which is wave 2's $100 threshold by another name and not a larger contrast; over damaged pairs it is $302.79.
treatment.dose_rule: treated = dose at or above the 90th percentile of the dose distribution over in-scope (disaster, county) pairs with a strictly positive recorded dose; control = dose below $1 per resident; pairs between the two are excluded
treatment.dose_timing: Damage is estimated by NWS offices from the physical event within weeks: a property of the shock, measured after it, but not derived from any employment outcome. As in wave 2 this is a disclosed use of an ex-post intensity, and the assumption that damage is not predicted by the county's employment path is what the leads test.
treatment.estimated_cohort_months_reason: The monthly first-release panel has national coverage from reference month 2007-05 and runs to 2026-07. A cohort needs its matching window at g-24 and its longest horizon at g+24, so 2009-05 is the earliest datable cohort and 2024-07 the latest. Every horizon is estimated on this one cohort set, so the four horizons are comparable rather than four different samples.
treatment.quiet_period_rule: a (disaster, county) pair is dropped when the county has another qualifying DR whose incident begins in the 36 months before g; other disasters in the same month or later are part of the post-period path
treatment.source: event_library: library_type fema_major_disaster_declaration (county rows, 50 states + DC); dose from noaa_storm_events county-coded damage; population from bea_national_regional CAINC1
treatment.timing: g = the calendar month of the disaster's incident_begin_date, indexed year * 12 + (month - 1)
treatment.treated_min_usd_per_capita_measured: Measured on treatment-side data only (FEMA declarations, NOAA county damage, BEA population) before any outcome was read. Pinned here as a number so that the design does not move if the sample does.

units.definition: (disaster, county) pairs: each disaster is a stack holding its treated and control counties; a county may appear in several stacks
units.notes: County definitional changes are not bridged. The two FRED aliases for Hancock County, KY are one county in the outcome panel, which keeps the earlier of the two releases for a month.
units.sample: units need the outcome in month g-24 and month g-13; others are dropped
units.strata: disaster x pre-growth half: comparisons are only within the same disaster and the same half of the outcome's growth from g-24 to g-13 (split at the median of the disaster's treated and control counties by (growth, id) rank)
units.strata_differs_from_wave_2: Wave 2 matched every outcome on employment growth. Here each outcome is matched on its own growth from g-24 to g-13, as units.strata says, so the secondary outcomes sit on partly different unit sets from the primary one and their samples are reported separately. This is the sample the power measurement was computed on, so it is kept rather than changed after the fact; the cost is that a secondary outcome is not a decomposition of the primary one.
units.unit_window: each unit's series is clipped to event months -24..+24 around its own stack's declaration month. Every unit belongs to exactly one declaration and every unit in a stack shares that declaration's month, so a month outside that window can enter no group-time cell this design estimates; the clip is exact, not an approximation.

windows.bounding_only_reason: Stated explicitly so no reader and no runner has to infer it from power.measured. It agrees with power.measured.verdict.can_only_bound_at, and the runner raises if the two ever disagree. Their minimum detectable effects clear 0.02, but the test rejects a true null 11.5% of the time at both, past the power registration's 10% limit, so no rejection at these horizons may be reported as an effect.
windows.e_min_reason: Leads e = -6..-2 are the gating pre-trend window, chosen on measured size before registration; see power.measured.diagnostics.why_the_lead_window_is_six_months. The matching window ends at g-13, so it still ends before every tested lead.
windows.horizons_note: All four horizons are estimated on the same cohort set and the same panel. The primary estimand is the mean ATT over event months 0..6: it is the longest horizon at which the design is both powered against the effect worth finding and correctly sized (measured minimum detectable effect 0.0116 against 0.02, rejection rate under a true null 9.0% against a 10% limit). The 3-month horizon is reported beside it. The 12- and 24-month horizons are registered as BOUNDING ONLY: their minimum detectable effects also clear 0.02, but the test rejects a true null 11.5% of the time at both, so no rejection at those horizons may be reported as an effect and their intervals must be read as wider than they print.

overall.definition: equal-weight mean of ATT(e) over the post event times listed

does_not_establish: Coverage before reference month 2007-05 is the Federal Reserve Eighth District, not the nation, which is why no cohort before 2009-05 is estimated: its matching window would fall in months when only seven states were in the archive.
A monthly outcome raises the number of periods, not the number of states. Inference is clustered on state, so the design's precision is bounded by roughly 50 clusters however many months it holds.

BOUNDING ONLY, never an effect, at these horizons: 12 months 11.5%, 24 months 11.5%. Those are the rates at which this design rejects a true null, measured before registration on synthetic panels with no effect in them, against a 10% limit. The intervals printed for those horizons are therefore narrower than their true coverage and must be read as wider than they print, and a rejection at them is not an effect and is not reported as one here. The registered primary estimand is the mean ATT over event months 0..6, the longest horizon at which this design is both powered against the effect worth finding and correctly sized.
